record.title: Brazilian education council opinion on national AI-use guidelines is homologated
record.summary: Brazil’s Ministry of Education homologated National Council of Education Opinion CNE/CP 15/2026 on national guidelines for using AI in education; the homologation dispatch appeared in the Federal Official Gazette on Nov 11. The opinion lays out guidance on human oversight of consequential decisions, risk-sensitive safeguards, student-data protection and age-specific use. Its annex contains a project resolution, and the opinion says a corresponding resolution is intended to provide normative effect. The reviewed sources do not establish publication of that standalone resolution, implementation or educational outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Brazilian Ministry of Education homologated CNE/CP Opinion 15/2026; the MEC-hosted opinion identifies the ministerial dispatch published in the Federal Official Gazette on 11 November 2026. The Council Plenary approved the opinion unanimously on 1 September 2026.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The homologated opinion sets out national guidance for educational uses of AI, including human responsibility for consequential educational decisions, risk-sensitive safeguards, protection of student data, and age-specific limits. Its annex includes a project resolution; the opinion says a corresponding resolution is intended to provide normative effect.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed sources do not establish that the standalone final resolution has been published or is in force, nor do they establish institutional compliance, implementation outcomes or effects on educational quality.

evidence_gaps.description: The standalone final resolution and its official publication/effective date were not located; the opinion’s annex is a project resolution.
Institutional adoption, compliance, educational outcomes and effects on students or providers are not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as described, nationwide education-sector AI guidelines can change institutional governance, student safeguards and vendor practices across Brazilian education. The opinion is homologated, but the attached resolution is still a project and implementation outcomes are unknown.
limitations: The homologated opinion and its attached project resolution are official primary sources, but the latter is not established here as an in-force standalone rule.
The press release says the proposed resolution sets a 12-month adaptation period from publication; its final legal text and start date remain unverified.
No institution-level implementation, compliance or education outcome is measured.

technical.claimed_result: The official opinion was homologated and contains national AI-in-education guidance; the final standalone resolution and implementation status remain to be checked.
technical.compute_or_cost: Not measured in the reviewed sources.
technical.demonstrated_result: MEC-hosted CNE/CP 15/2026 opinion bearing the “PARECER HOMOLOGADO” heading and ministerial DOU dispatch reference dated Nov 11, 2026; the CNE decision section records unanimous approval on Sep 1, 2026.
technical.implementation_status: Opinion homologated; attached resolution remains a project in the text. Publication/effect of a standalone final resolution was not verified.
technical.mechanism: The opinion supplies principles, risk classifications and proposed safeguards for AI use across education levels; its attached project resolution sets out a proposed regulatory structure.
technical.novelty: The homologation advances a national Brazilian AI-in-education policy process from CNE approval to ministerial homologation.
technical.regime: Brazilian education systems and institutions, spanning basic and higher education; legal implementation and local adaptation remain unverified.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to this policy act.
technical.strongest_baseline: Earlier CNE approval and Oct 6 DOU summary preceded ministerial homologation; the homologation dispatch is dated Nov 11.

brief.why_it_matters: A nationwide framework could shape AI governance, student protections and vendor practices across Brazilian schools and higher-education institutions. The approved opinion is material policy direction, while operative timing and implementation remain unresolved.
